summary: Map PID tunability vs load inertia: overshoot grids, braking-window theory, per-load tuning recipe

mapper.summary: Mapped snap-step (0.2 rot) overshoot vs tuning vs inertia for fw 0.15.4.1 semantics (--alg step2 --i-gate avg --i-gate-freeze-unwind --i-gate-stale-ticks 6250) across J x{1,5,20,50} x kp{60..2000} x kd{175k..5.6M} x ki{0,25} x 3 seeds (864 step runs + 864 standstill probes + 180 ki-sweep runs + 21 16-s runs + 360 finalist runs = 2,289 runs, overflow_violations=0 in every single run). Result: near-zero overshoot (<2,000 counts) is achievable ONLY at J x1 and J x5. J x1 floor ~1,100-1,400 counts (kp2000/kd700k/ki25: med 1184, max 1216, settle 0.17 s, quiet). J x5 floor ~1,200-1,400 (kp500/kd1.4M/ki25: med 1251, max 1406, settle up to 4 s). J x20: kp500/kd1.4M reaches 1,781-2,029 counts BUT always leaves a persistent 3.8 Hz ~1,500-count limit cycle (persists >=16 s, at every ki 1..25); the only robustly quiet J x20 cell (kp2000/kd350k) overshoots 65,740 counts (7.2 deg) and itself breaks into a 5,000-count hunt after a tiny step or load release. J x50 minimum: 10,434-11,881 counts (kp250/kd5.6M, hunting) or 15,369-16,934 (kp250/kd1.4M, quiet in ~2/3 of seeds, hunt GROWS over 16 s in the rest). H1 confirmed quantitatively: overshoot at kp2000 tracks the stopping-distance-minus-window bound (J20: predicted >=40k, observed 67k; J50: predicted >=54k, observed 82k; J1: window > stopping distance, observed only ~1.2k), and lowering kp helps monotonically down to a knee at kp~500 (J5/J20) / kp~250 (J50), below which overshoot rises again. H2 refined: the pure D-noise ceiling (ki=0) is kd~2.8M-5.6M (max_error_change ~ 1 sigma) and RISES with J (J50 never noise-hunts); the kd>=2.8M hunting Tom saw on the bench matches the ki=25 map, where the cycle is integral-driven stick-slip (same cells dead quiet at ki=0), so the operative ceiling with integral action is kd<=1.4M and it FALLS with J. ki=0 gives zero overshoot at any J but parks 6,200-410,000 counts off target (offset ~12.6M/kp counts) - unusable. The knee overshoot is ki-insensitive (ki 1..25 within ~15%), and lowering ki does NOT cure the high-J limit cycle. High-J rescue is trajectory shaping, not tuning: the sim reproduces Tom's bench finding (slower move-time fixes it), and at J50 the 0.05-s profiled move is dynamically infeasible (needs 320 rev/s^2 vs available 235), giving 88k overshoot regardless of gains.
mapper.verdict: H1 CONFIRMED (braking-window blindness sets the high-kp overshoot floor; knee where window ~ 2-4x stopping distance). H2 PARTIALLY CONFIRMED (a kd noise ceiling exists at max_error_change ~ sigma i.e. kd ~2.8M, but it rises with J at ki=0; the bench kd>=2.8M hunting is the integral-driven stick-slip cycle, which ki 1-25 all sustain at J>=20). H3 REJECTED at high J within current firmware: no tuning at J x20/x50 gives both low overshoot and quiet settling on a snap step. Min achievable snap overshoot: J x1 ~1.2k counts (0.13 deg, robust), J x5 ~1.3k (0.14 deg, robust), J x20 ~1.9k but only with a permanent 1.5k-count 3.8 Hz limit cycle (quiet alternative: 66k), J x50 ~10-17k counts (1.2-1.9 deg, seed-bimodal hunting risk). <2,000 counts: YES at J x1/x5, NO at J x20 (marginal on overshoot, fails quiet), NO at J x50.

DELIVERABLE 2 - H1 OVERSHOOT-vs-KP (median ov, ki=25, kd=1.4M): J x1: kp2000:1208 kp1000:1181 kp500:2857 kp250:7565 kp125:5199 kp60:2934 (no window limit - flat floor, window 52,428 > stopping distance 14,100 even at kp2000). J x5: 40431 / 20045 / 1251 / 5660 / 37704 / 10642 - monotonic improvement 2000->500, KNEE at kp500, worse below. J x20: 67563 / 45555 / 1818 / 8839 / 58441 / 26756 - knee kp500. J x50: 82115 / 59470 / 15948 / 16851 / 70174 / 37921 - knee kp250-500 (at kd5.6M J50 keeps falling to kp250: 11153). QUANTITATIVE H1 CHECK at kp2000 (window w=104,857,600/kp=52,428 counts; stopping s=J*w_entry^2/(2*0.4)): J x5 vel_at_linear_entry 32.1M counts/s -> s=66,800, predicted ov >= s-w = 14,400, observed 40,431; J x20: 18.9M -> s=92,800, predicted >=40,400, observed 67,563; J x50: 12.8M -> s=106,400, predicted >=54,000, observed 82,115. Observed = 1.5-2.8x the hard geometric bound (I-term and soft braking account for the rest). Below the knee overshoot rises again because the window already exceeds stopping distance and lower kp only softens linear-regime stiffness while I dominates. H1 mechanism CONFIRMED; 'monotonic' holds only above the knee.

DELIVERABLE 3 - KD HUNT CEILING (H2): Standstill-from-rest NEVER hunts in this sim (std=33 for all 288 combos - stick-slip parks it; bench standstill hunting needs prior excitation). Operative map = post-step last-1s std (>200 = hunting). ki=0 (pure D-noise ceiling): kd<=2.8M quiet at ALL J and kp; kd=5.6M hunts only at low kp (J1: kp<=125 std 924-1757; J5: kp<=250; J20: kp60 only; J50: never). max_error_change at kd2.8M = 37 counts ~ 1.1 sigma(33), at 5.6M = 18 ~ 0.55 sigma -> ceiling sits where authority/kd ~ sigma as H2 predicted, BUT it RISES with J (inertia low-passes the noise torque), opposite of naive expectation. ki=25: hunting everywhere at kd>=2.8M (std 391-1,914 at every J including J x1 - matches Tom's bench 'kd>=2.8M hunted'), plus kd=175k hunts fast (underdamped, std 2k-4k), plus at J>=20 nearly ALL cells limit-cycle (std 1,200-2,700 at 3.8-4.1 Hz). Same cells at ki=0 are silent -> the bench hunting is an INTEGRAL-driven stick-slip cycle that kd dither sustains (D prevents re-stick), not pure D-noise saturation. Operative quiet corridor with ki=25: J x1 kd 350k-1.4M (any kp), J x5 only ~4 cells (kd 350k-1.4M, kp-dependent), J x20 one cell, J x50 scattered bimodal islands.

KI FINDINGS (off-grid sweep ki {1,2,5,10,25} at knee cells, 10-s runs, 3 seeds; ki_sweep.py output in transcript): (a) the overshoot floor is ki-insensitive - J x1 kp2000/kd700k: 1315/1179/1274/1206/1175 for ki 1/2/5/10/25 (matches bench 'ki0 vs ki25 within 15%'); (b) lowering ki does NOT cure the high-J limit cycle: J x20 kp500/kd1.4M std stays 1,431-1,550 even at ki=1; (c) it only slows settling (J x1 settle 1.20 s at ki1 vs 0.17 s at ki25); (d) ki=0 parks off by ~12.6M/kp counts (kp2000: ~6,200 counts = 0.68 deg; kp250: ~50,000 = 5.5 deg; measured medians in gridmaps_output.txt) - the ki=0 'zero overshoot' cells never cross zero at all, they stop short. Accuracy floor with ki=25 is the gate deadband: several cells park anywhere inside +/-1000 counts (last1s mean up to ~930) and my strict settle metric shows inf for those - metric artifact worth knowing, not instability.

DELIVERABLE 4 - EXPLICIT ANSWER (min achievable snap-step overshoot, current firmware, rigid load): J x1 (5.4e-6): YES, <2,000 counts robustly; min ~1,100-1,400 (0.12-0.15 deg) at kp2000/kd700k/ki25; nothing tested beat ~1,100. J x5 (2.7e-5): YES; min 1,197-1,406 at kp500/kd1.4M/ki25 (settle up to 4 s; kp250/kd1.4M is the fast-settling fallback at 5.7k). J x20 (1.08e-4): NO with acceptable behavior - kp500/kd1.4M straddles the line (1,781-2,029) but is inseparable from a permanent 1,500-count 3.8 Hz hunt at every ki tried; min QUIET overshoot is 65,740 (7.2 deg, kp2000/kd350k) and even that cell hunts after tiny steps/release. J x50 (2.7e-4): NO - absolute min 10,434-11,881 (kp250/kd5.6M, always hunting) or 15,369-16,934 (kp250/kd1.4M, quiet in most seeds, hunt grows in others). The 2,000-count target is missed by 5-8x.

FINALIST SCENARIOS B-F (5 seeds, finals_output.txt): B (bench snap: --move 0.2 --move-time 0.05): J x1 kp2000/kd700k ov med 1,106 - clean; J x5 kp500/kd1.4M ov ~5,600 (profiled 0.05-s move is HARSHER than the pure step at J>=5); J x20 kp500/kd1.4M ov ~17k; J x50 kp250/kd1.4M ov ~88k and kp1000/kd1.4M 242k - the 0.05-s triangular profile demands ~320 rev/s^2 decel vs tau/J = 235 rev/s^2 available at J x50: infeasible trajectory, no tuning can fix it; matches Tom's bench result that move-time 0.2 s collapses overshoot to ~0. C (2-rot/2-s tracking): quiet cells give post_move_rms 47-155 counts (J x1 all three, J x20 kp2000/kd350k, J x5 kp1000/kd700k); limit-cycle cells give 1,270-2,810. D (8-s standstill): std 33, max|err| <=150 for ALL finalists - dormancy is universally clean from rest. E (0.2 N*m hold, release at 3 s): release fix behaves at J x1 (peak 4.7-5.0k, settle 0.12 s) and mostly at J x5 (med 3.6k; one seed 21k); at J x20/x50 the release itself is small (peak med 3.7-7.2k) but drops the system into the persistent hunt (release_settle never, std 1.2-5.0k) except kp2000/kd350k J x20 whose release peak is 13-18k. F (0.001-rot Tom step): J x1 ~1.2k (i.e. overshoots its own step size - I-term dominated), J x5 ~1.5-1.9k, J x20/x50 2.6-6.7k AND wakes the limit cycle at J>=20 in every finalist.

CAVEATS / HONEST LIMITS: (1) plant is a RIGID inertia - the bench disk's backlash/compliance is unmodeled, so bench overshoot (18.5 deg at kp2000) is far worse than sim J x20-50 at the same gains (6-10 deg); trends (kp direction, kd>=2.8M hunting, move-time rescue) reproduce, absolute counts will not. (2) Stick-slip outcomes ARE bimodal as warned - J x50 kp250/kd1.4M and J x20 kp2000/kd350k(ki10) flip quiet/hunting by seed; per-seed numbers reported above. (3) The step2+avg-gate integral parks anywhere inside the 1000-count gate deadband, so 'settled accuracy' is ~0.1 deg worst case regardless of tuning. (4) Standstill hunt probes from rest are blind to the operative instability; use post-excitation std instead (I did). RECOMMENDED per-load defaults if Tom wants them: bare rotor kp2000/ki25/kd700k; ~5x inertia kp500/ki25/kd1.4M; >=20x inertia: no good snap tuning exists - use kp500/kd1.4M ONLY with profiled moves sized to tau/J, or accept 7-deg-class overshoot at kp2000/kd350k; firmware-side, the two levers this map points at are (a) making the braking window velocity-aware (H1 blindness) and (b) breaking the I-driven stick-slip cycle at high J (the avg-gate midpoint rule does not kill it).

archprobe.summary: Quantified both architectural clamps on scratch copies of pid_algorithm_sim.c (fw 0.15.4.1 semantics, 576-run grid: 3 J x 4 kp x 4 kd x 3 seeds x 4 architectures, --step 0.2, ki 25). H1 (error window = authority/kp) is CONFIRMED as the diagnosis of the heavy-load kp2000 overshoot (measured overshoot matches J*w^2/(2*tau_brake) - window within ~10%), but the proposed remedy FAILS: in this architecture the window clamp is the braking trigger (P clamped at +authority is cancelled by mec-railed D at -authority at the window edge), so widening it to 8x makes overshoot catastrophically WORSE at kp>=500 (up to 47 deg at J50) via un-cancellable P plus gain-1 back-calc slamming I to the wrong rail. H2 is CONFIRMED and its fix is the winner: stock usable kd ceils at ~1.4M (mec=74 counts/tick ~ 1.6 sigma of hall-noise error-change; kd>=5.6M becomes a noise bang-bang, hunting 2.7-4.2 Hz at every J, matching the bench), while unclamped int64 velocity-D moves the ceiling up with inertia: at J50 it is the only architecture that is simultaneously on-target, quiet (last-1s std 228-435 counts) and low-overshoot (0.17-0.23 deg vs stock's best-quiet 1.8 deg) - a 9x improvement - and it also improves hold-release peaks 3-4x. At bare J the stock architecture is already at its friction/noise floor (0.19 deg quiet) and velocity-D is slightly worse there (must derate kd to 350k -> 0.29 deg). Honest negatives: several "0 overshoot" veld cells at J1/J20 are fake (rotor hangs short of target, never crosses zero); at J20 with ki=25 no architecture is both quiet and low-overshoot (stick-slip limit cycle, not the clamps, is the limiter - ki sweep is the follow-up). Zero overflow_violations in all 576 runs; the int64 requirements for a velocity-D firmware change are itemized.
archprobe.verdict: Firmware change worth pursuing: YES, but only the velocity-based D input (unclamped int64 error_change + int64 P+I+D sum), and only as an optional/tunable mode - it buys ~9x lower overshoot at 50x inertia (0.2 deg quiet vs 1.8 deg stock-quiet; stock is NOT within 1.5x of its achievable floor at heavy J) and better release behavior, at the cost of a lower usable-kd at bare rotor (retune per load, which matches Tom's per-load-tuning requirement). The wider error-clamp cap (H1 remedy) should NOT be pursued: it removes the architecture's emergent braking trigger and interacts destructively with gain-1 back-calculation (24-50 deg overshoots at kp>=500); lowering kp already widens the window within the stock architecture and reaches 1.2-1.8 deg at J50. The pure physics floor (bang-bang, full visibility) is ~0 for a 0.2-rot step at every tested J, so the honest benchmark is stock-best vs relaxed-best: J1 1.4x (stock fine), J20 ~1.2x (both limited by ki-25 stick-slip, not clamps), J50 9.1x (architecture-limited, velocity-D fixes it).

WIDE-WINDOW FAILURE MECHANISM (trace wide_trace.csv vs stock_trace.csv, J50 kp2000/kd1.4M seed1): stock at t=step+1ms: P=+104.86M (clamped at authority), D->-102.2M (mec-railed), so by t=+20ms output collapses to 14,076 of 51,200 rail (graduated braking at the window edge) and peak overshoot is 52.4k. wide: P=8x authority=838.9M, D still authority-limited cannot cancel it, output pinned at full +51,200 deep into the approach, and gain-1 back-calc slams I to -104.86M then to +104.86M after the cross (wrong-way drive); overshoot 428.5k cts = 47 deg (per-seed 428,516-428,561). The stock max_error clamp is not merely a blindness bug - it is the de-facto brake trigger of this architecture; H1's remedy is rejected. H2 NOISE CEILING QUANTIFIED: hall sigma 33 -> error_change noise sigma ~47/tick. Stock mec = authority/kd: 300 cts (kd350k, 6.4sigma, never binds), 74 (1.4M, 1.6sigma), 18 (5.6M, 0.39sigma), 4 (22.4M, 0.086sigma). The ceiling moves up with J exactly as H3 predicted, giving veld ~16x more usable damping authority at J50 (kd 22.4M vs 1.4M).

HONESTY / FAKE ZEROS: overshoot_counts only counts after the error crosses zero. veld/both cells reporting 0 overshoot at J1 kd>=1.4M and J20 kp125/kd22.4M are rotors HANGING SHORT of target (last-1s mean error 11.9k-650k cts) - excluded from all 'best' claims above. Verified genuine winners sit on target: J50 veld kp500/kd22.4M last-1s mean -17..+9 cts; J50 both kp2000/kd22.4M mean -5..+13, std 36-97.

RELEASE REGRESSION CHECK (J50, --load 0.1 --load-until 3, seeds 1-3): stock kp250/kd5.6M release_peak_err 2447-3880 cts, never settles (<1000 sustained) due to its limit cycle; veld kp500/kd22.4M release_peak 462-1035, settles in 0.00-0.13 s. Velocity-D does not regress the fw 0.15.4.1 release fix - it improves it 3-4x at heavy J.

INT32/OVERFLOW IMPLICATIONS FOR A FUTURE Sec.21 (from instrumented i32_sum_overflows shadow counter): (a) velocity-D: |D| pre-shift reaches ~1.1e10-3.8e10 (2^33.4-2^35.1) at saturated approach speeds (error_change up to ~1678 cts/tick at 16 rev/s x 32-tick LPF x deriv_scaled 700k at kd22.4M) -> the LPF state, D term, and P+I+D sum MUST be int64; the int32 sum would have overflowed on up to 150k of 187.5k ticks (80%) in the worst cell (J1 kd22.4M). Post-shift output fits int32; back-calc correction is already int64 in firmware, and the tick path already uses int64 (ni, correction) so MCU precedent exists - budget a few extra soft-int64 ops per tick and re-measure ISR headroom. Keep a sanity clamp on error_change at PID_MAX_ERROR_CHANGE=2e6 (wrap protection) instead of authority/kd. (b) gain-1 back-calc must be revisited for D-driven saturation: with unlimited D the excess routinely slams I to +/-full rail (peak_i_pct=100 in all veld cells); it behaved acceptably in sim but a bounded correction (or back-calc only on P+I-driven saturation) is the safer firmware form. (c) wide-window (rejected anyway): 8*authority = 838,860,800 fits int32 only because the M17 authority cap is at V=200; on products with the 800e6 authority cap 8x would overflow int32 outright. (d) ki_effective overflow cap logic self-adapts to a wider max_error (verified: ki=25 uncapped at all grid points).

CAVEATS: sim load is RIGID - the bench disk is loose/backlash, so absolute overshoot numbers (esp. the 0.17-0.23 deg veld figures) will degrade on the bench; the architectural conclusion (stock kd-ceiling is J-independent, veld ceiling scales with J) should hold directionally. ki fixed at 25 per task spec: the J20 residual oscillation in ALL architectures (std ~900-1900, osc 3-4 Hz) and the J50 stock hunting are ki-driven stick-slip cycles - a ki (and i-gate deadband) sweep at heavy J is the highest-value follow-up before committing to any firmware change. TASK 2a — EXTENDED SEEDS (1-12, step 0.2): J1 rec ov 1105-1252 settle <=0.25 s, fully robust. J5 rec ov 1176-1406; 3/12 seeds read settle=inf but two are the park-at-edge metric artifact (mean 910/933, std 33 — parked just inside the 1000-count deadband) and one is a marginal 0.4 Hz wander (std 836). NEW default-comparator finding: at J5 the CURRENT DEFAULT kp2000/ki25/kd350k both overshoots 33.7-33.9k counts (3.7 deg) AND limit-cycles permanently (std ~2539, 4.2 Hz, sustained >=16 s, 12/12 seeds) after a 0.2-rot snap; at J50 default gives 97.0-97.8k (10.7 deg) + permanent 5k-count cycle. J50 rec: ov unchanged 15.4-17.6k (24 seeds, no tail) but now hunts 5/5 (std ~1382). J50 ALT kp250/kd5.6M: seed 4 overshoots 217,567 counts = 23.9 deg (deterministic, reproduced twice; peak_vel 5.71 vs 3.24 rev/s in sibling seeds) — 1/24 seeds; mechanism: max_error_change = authority/kd = 18 counts ~ 0.55 sigma, so D is a noise bang-bang during approach and occasionally fails to brake at the reduced breakaway friction. J1 rec: ov 1262-1926, develops a slow ~0.2-0.4 Hz wander std 419-531 (default kd350k stays quiet at std 66 with ov ~2627) — at J1 the default is MORE noise-robust; if the bench is noisier than sigma 33, use kd350k at J1. J5 rec: ov 1849-2244 but now limit-cycles (std ~1314, 3.3-4.0 Hz; default: ov 34283 + std 2499 — rec still better on both). J20 rec: ov ~5960, std 2274. J50 rec: ov 24.1-27.5k and std explodes to 14.9-16.5k counts (1.7 deg!) at 4.4 Hz — 3x WORSE residual motion than default (std ~5030) though overshoot stays 4x better; J50 alt similar (std ~15.3k). TASK 2d — STEP SIZES: 0.02 rot: J1 rec 1134-1217 clean; J5 rec 1241-1362 (park-at-edge artifacts); J20 rec ov ~1828 + usual hunt; J50 rec ov ~6917 + now hunts 3/3 (small steps leave J50 rec in the cycle more reliably than big ones); DEFAULT at J5/J20/J50 hunts after this tiny step too (std 2539/5025/5048, def J20 ov 12054 on a 65,536-count step). 0.61 rot: J1 rec 1149-1231 still clean; J5 rec 1481-1632 still clean (window 209,715 counts absorbs it); J20/J50: CATASTROPHIC for every tuning — J20 rec 262,700 (28.9 deg) vs def 229,042 (rec WORSE by 15%); J50 rec 636,951 vs def 700,997 vs alt 654,729 (57-77 deg). 2.0 rot: J1 rec 11,877 ~ def 11,741 (~1.3 deg both — approach speed saturates and exceeds even J1's braking window); J5 rec 53,250; J20/J50 240-533k all tunings. J1 rec: relpeak 4283-5059, settles 0.11-0.12 s (1/12 'no-settle' is the park-at-edge artifact: mean -932, std 33); better than def (5346-5557). J5 rec: relpeak med 3640 but max 21,058 (2.3 deg) in 1/12 seeds (settles 0.65 s); def relpeak 10,810 + never settles. J20 rec: relpeak med 7641, max 23,433, 6/12 never settle (drop into the limit cycle); def relpeak 16,121, 3/3 never settle — even the 'quiet' def hunts after release at nominal stiction. J50 rec: relpeak med 6396, max 29,831, 12/12 never settle (standing ~2.6k cycle); def relpeak 8284 no-settle. At --load 0.30 (75% authority): J1/J5 rec fine (relpeak 23.2k/5.0k, settle ~0.12 s); J50 shows a real trade — def relpeak 30.9k but then QUIET (settle 0.19 s, std 33) while rec relpeak 7.8k but never settles (std 2561). Report to Tom: rec = smaller release kick, def = cleaner aftermath at J50.

TASK 2f — PROFILED MOVES: 2-rot/2-s tracking: J1 rec postrms 75-172 vs def 33-67 (2.6x worse but absolutely negligible); J5 rec postrms med 436 vs def 66 — DEF IS QUIET after profiled moves at J5 even though it hunts after snaps; J20 rec postrms ~1583 (hunts) vs def 47 (quiet); J50 rec ~2787 (hunts) vs def 128 (quiet). 0.2-rot/50-ms (bench snap): J1 rec ov ~1115 movepeak 2775 (def 979/4973); J5 rec ov ~5585 ~ def 5385 but def then hunts (postrms 2565); J20 rec ov 17.6k + 2/3 hunt vs def 28.9k ov but clean recovery (std 33, settle 0.07); J50 rec 89.2k vs def 288.7k vs alt 104.5k — all bad, trajectory infeasible, matches mapper. 0.2-rot/200-ms: J1/J5 rec ~1001-1218 clean; J20 rec ov 1778 but 2/3 hunt vs def 3955 quiet settle 0.17 s; J50 rec ov 11.5k (2/3 hunt std 2703) vs def ov 7913 + permanent std 5058. AMENDMENT: at J>=20 the rec gains are for snap duty only; for profiled motion the default class (kp2000/kd350k) is flatly better at J20 and better-behaved at J50 tracking — per-duty gain scheduling or the mapper's 'profile the move' advice should be the headline for heavy loads.

TASK 2g — STANDSTILL 20 s: all 10 cells identical and clean (std 33, |mean| 0, maxerr 147-168, osc 0) — dormancy from rest is universally safe; no tuning self-excites without prior excitation. TASK 2h — KI ROBUSTNESS (5/10/25/50/100, 10-s runs): J1 rec: ov 1121-1367, settle <=0.32 s, std 33 at ALL ki — fully robust, Tom can change ki freely at J1. J5 rec: ov 1158-1424 at all ki (insensitive) but settle stretches to ~7.6 s at ki10 and parks at the deadband edge more often at low ki; no hunting except one marginal std 808 at ki10. J5 alt: 4428-6551 stable. J20 rec: hunts at EVERY ki (std 1461-1797; cycle frequency scales with ki: 2.0-2.1 Hz at ki5 -> 4.5 Hz at ki100; ov stable 1684-2233) — lowering ki does not cure it, confirming the mapper. J20 def: quiet only at ki>=25 (at ki5/10 1-2 of 3 seeds hunt, std up to 4186) — another fragility of the 'quiet' pick. J50 rec: hunts at every ki and std GROWS with ki: 2253 (ki5) / 2340 (ki10) / ~2600 (ki25) / 3553 (ki50) / 8639 (ki100 = 0.95 deg std!); ov 14.4-19.1k mildly improves with ki. J50 alt: same shape, std 6171 at ki100. AMENDMENT: J50 rec carries 'ki<=25' as a hard caveat; J20 def carries 'ki>=25'.

TASK 3 — GATE AT LOW KP (kp125 P-term gives output 125*1000>>11=61 counts -> voltage 61>>8=0 at the deadband edge; P alone produces zero torque below ~4200 counts of error, so final convergence is I-driven): At J1/J5 kp125 converges but slowly — parks anywhere within +/-900 counts, settle 3-6+ s (J1 kd1.4M med 6.23 s), ov 3.2-10.4k, and kd5.6M hunts (std 845-1039). At J20/J50 with weak kd it is catastrophic: J20 kp125/kd350k std 26,525-26,936 (2.9 deg limit cycle, 4.6 Hz); J50 kp125/kd350k std ~53,525 with last-1s MEAN -3,888 — parked OUTSIDE the deadband, error never converges; J50 kp125/kd1.4M on-target (mean -8) but permanent std 2706; kp60/kd1.4M: ov 26.8k/37.9k + permanent hunt at J20/J50. Release at kp125 heavy J (momentum >> integral): relpeak 4.1-8.3k at both 0.2 and 0.30 N*m — the stale-crossing/freeze-unwind fix holds even when P is torque-less; failures are 'falls into the standing cycle', never a windup runaway. Hold-under-load at kp125/J50: 1/3 seeds hunts while loaded (std 8570, mean 3501). CONCLUSION: the gate itself is not the low-kp hazard (its deadband parking is kp-independent as suspected, ~0.1 deg worst case); the hazard is I-driven limit cycling once P is inside its zero-voltage band — floor recommendations at kp>=250, and expect multi-second I-crawl settling below kp~500.

TASK 4 — SCENARIOS WHERE A RECOMMENDED SET IS WORSE THAN DEFAULT kp2000/ki25/kd350k (complete list): J1 rec kd700k: (1) 2x noise residual motion — std 419-531 + 0.2-0.4 Hz wander vs def's quiet 66; (2) 2-rot snap ov 11,877 vs 11,741 (1% worse, both ~1.3 deg); (3) profiled 2-rot tracking postrms 75-172 vs 33-67 counts (negligible). J5 rec kp500/kd1.4M: (4) profiled 2-rot tracking postrms med 436 vs 66 (def is quiet after profiled moves at J5); (5) settle character — parks near deadband edge over 2-4 s (up to 7.6 s at ki10) vs def's fast park when def happens to be quiet; everything else rec wins big (def at J5: 33.9k ov + permanent hunt). J20 rec kp500/kd1.4M: (6) permanent 1.5k-count cycle after ANY excitation vs def quiet-at-nominal (but def's quiet is conditional — fails at stiction 0.03, noise 66, ki<=10, steps <=0.02 or >=0.61 rot, and after releases); (7) 0.61-rot snap ov 262.7k vs 229.0k; (8) 2.0-rot 255.2k vs 244.7k; (9) profiled tracking postrms 1583 vs 47; (10) 50-ms and 200-ms move aftermath — def recovers clean (std 33) where rec keeps hunting. J50 rec kp250/kd1.4M: (11) profiled 2-rot tracking postrms 2787 vs 128; (12) 200-ms move ov 11.5k vs 7.9k (but def then hunts at 5k std, rec at 2.7k — mixed); (13) release-0.30 aftermath — def settles quiet in 0.19 s (relpeak 30.9k) vs rec never settles (relpeak 7.8k); (14) 2x-noise residual std 15.5k vs 5.0k (3x worse). J50 alt kd5.6M: removed — worse than default in tail risk (217k = 2.2x def's 97k worst case) despite better median.

SIM-VS-BENCH HONESTY: all of this is the RIGID-load sim; Tom's disk has backlash, so absolute counts will not transfer (bench 18.5 deg at kp2000 vs sim J20-50 6-11 deg at same gains) — but every bench trend the mapper cited reproduces here (kp direction, kd>=2.8M-class hunting via ki-driven stick-slip, move-time rescue, ki insensitivity of the overshoot floor within 15%). Second sim caveat: park-at-edge settle=inf readings are a metric artifact (rotor parked at 900-980 counts inside the 1000-count gate deadband with std 33) — I verified each 'inf' against last1s mean/std before calling anything unstable; the +/-1000-count (0.11 deg) parking is the accuracy floor of the shipped gate at ANY tuning and any kp. Third: two-seed-level rare events (the 217k tail, the 21-30k release peaks) were found only because of 12-24-seed sweeps; bench validation of the J50 recommendation should run >=10 repetitions before trusting any single number. Sim doc nit worth fixing in repo: usage() says noise default 18 / static 0.060, code says 33 / 0.13.

BOTTOM LINE FOR TOM'S REQUIREMENT ('a set of PID parameters per load, tunable for any kind of load'): TRUE at bare rotor and ~5x inertia — kp2000/ki25/kd700k and kp500/ki25/kd1.4M deliver ~0.13-0.15 deg snap overshoot robustly (ki-flexible 5-100, stiction-insensitive, amplitude-tolerant to ~0.6 rot). FALSE at >=20x inertia within current firmware for snap duty: every tuning either overshoots >=7 deg or carries a permanent 1.5-2.7k-count limit cycle that any disturbance re-wakes, and ki/kp/kd sweeps (60..2000 x 175k..22.4M x 1..100 across mapper+archprobe+this validation) found no escape; the workable heavy-load answer remains trajectory shaping (0.2-s profiled moves collapse overshoot to ~0.05 deg on bench and in sim) plus, if firmware work is approved, the archprobe's velocity-D direction (which this validation did not re-test — repo-source semantics only). The braking-window arithmetic (H1) and the integral-driven stick-slip mechanism (H2 refinement) survived every adversarial scenario I could throw at them.
